domain: Intellectual Property Law / Technology Governance / Information Economics
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested legal boundary of 'derivative work' under copyright law, where the statutory kernel is read expansively by incumbent rightsholders (maximizing enclosure over downstream creative acts) versus narrowly by generative AI proponents and transformative use advocates (protecting coordination scaffolds for new creation). The disagreement concerns what the statutory constraint itself permits, not merely policy preference.

key_entities: Generative AI developers (OpenAI, Stability AI, etc.)
key_tensions: Expansive reading (any use of expression is derivative) vs narrow reading (only fixed recastings are derivative)
Enclosure maximization (rightsholder control over training/transformation) vs coordination scaffold (public domain expansion via non-infringing uses)
key_mechanisms: Licensing requirement (rightsholders extract rents from derivative uses)
Fair use doctrine (judicial escape valve for transformative uses)
key_absences: Statutory definition does not specify whether intermediate/ephemeral uses (e.g., ML training) constitute 'preparation' of derivative work
No explicit treatment of probabilistic transformation vs deterministic recasting

axes.structural_delta: Any use of copyrighted expression in creating new work constitutes preparation of derivative work requiring authorization
axes.primary_observable: Licensing requirements enforced; injunctions against ML training; statutory damages awarded for unauthorized transformative use
axes.selection_reason: Core contested reading; instantiates high-extraction constraint with clear beneficiary/victim structure

axes.structural_delta: Only fixed recastings that substantially incorporate original expression constitute derivative works; transformative and intermediate uses are non-infringing
axes.primary_observable: Fair use defenses succeed; ML training held non-infringing; transformative works proliferate without licensing
axes.selection_reason: Competing reading with structurally opposite constraint (low ε coordination vs high ε extraction)

axes.structural_delta: Derivative work boundary depends on commercial exploitation: non-commercial transformative use permitted; commercial use requires authorization
axes.primary_observable: Split outcomes in fair use cases by commerciality; statutory amendment proposals distinguishing commercial ML training
axes.selection_reason: Third structurally distinct reading attempting to reconcile poles via categorical carveout; instantiates partial extraction

axes.structural_delta: Derivative work requires fixation in tangible medium; intermediate/ephemeral uses (e.g., ML training without storing copies) are non-derivative
axes.primary_observable: Court holdings on RAM copies; transitory use doctrine applications
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: technical doctrinal refinement of coordination_reading; lower independent structural yield

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Three readings pass independence test with distinct observables and epsilon structures. Kernel recognition coherent: statutory ambiguity licenses plural readings, each instantiating different constraint type.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: 17 U.S.C. § 101 definition of 'derivative work' as 'work based upon one or more preexisting works' — statutory text claimed as fixed reference point for legitimate copyright enforcement
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Federal judiciary holds final interpretive authority via case law; Copyright Office issues administrative guidance; rightsholders claim interpretive legitimacy via statutory language and legislative history

readings.commitment: Any use of copyrighted expression in creating new work constitutes preparation of derivative work
readings.authority_grounding: Textual maximalism — 'based upon' read broadly; rightsholder economic interest as interpretive lens; legislative history emphasizing author control
readings.expected_structural_delta: High ε snare: licensing requirements enforced pre-creation; downstream innovation bottlenecked; extraction flows to incumbents

readings.commitment: Only fixed recastings substantially incorporating original expression are derivative works; transformative and intermediate uses non-infringing
readings.authority_grounding: Purposivist — copyright promotes progress via incentives, not maximal control; fair use doctrine as co-equal interpretive principle; First Amendment considerations
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low ε rope: no ex-ante licensing requirement for transformative use; ML training permissible; coordination scaffold for generative technologies

readings.commitment: Derivative work boundary varies by commercial exploitation: non-commercial transformative use permitted; commercial use requires authorization
readings.authority_grounding: Pragmatic balancing — fair use statutory factors (purpose/character, market effect) as interpretive heuristic; judicial reluctance to choose absolute rule
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate ε tangled_rope: commercial developers face licensing costs; non-commercial users exempt; partial extraction with categorical beneficiary split

axiom_contradictions.basis: Enclosure reading treats copyright as property right maximally excludable against all uses absent consent (Lockean/natural rights axiom). Coordination reading treats copyright as limited utilitarian grant subordinate to public interest in access and transformation (consequentialist/public goods axiom). No single coherent framework holds both: property absolutism and consequentialist balancing are mutually exclusive normative foundations.
